title: Laal Durbeen
subtitle: Rosy Colored Glasses
paragraphs: On a random Tuesday, Prem left his small apartment at the end of Jhormuda street in Ranchi. He was on the journey of a lifetime, at least so was the perception in his eyes. As he headed to the train station, someone called his name from behind
Aarju - ‘Prem bhaiya….Prem bhaiya’

Prem was a man in his late 30s with a slight slouch and a lean body. He carried a pair of red binoculars with him everywhere. He was infamous in his neighbourhood as the ‘laal durbin wala’ / the man with red binoculars.
Prem turned back and found the young boy Aarju waving his hands in the air, trying to get his attention.
Prem - ‘Aarju beta, I am headed on a long journey. I will talk to you when I am back’
Aarju was the son of the cigarette seller of the neighbourhood. He was a naughty, yet helpful boy who spent most of his time flying kites and chasing street dogs.
Aarju - ‘Look what I found, bhaiya wait! Prem bhaiya wait!’

Prem saw his train approaching the station and looking at the crowd in front of him, he decided to focus on catching the train instead of the constant calling of Aarju. Prem said to himself, ‘Oh this boy is definitely up to a new menace, he is going to make me miss my train. I better run before it is too late’
With this resolve in his mind, Prem rushed with his handbag in one hand and his one-way ticket in the other. It was after all the journey of a lifetime, how can he miss it?
His train left the station the same time Aarju reached the platform. He kept shouting, ‘Prem bhaiya, Prem bhaiya look what I found’
But it was too late, this treasure that Aarju had found had to wait for Prem to return.

Prem lived alone in a small room above the cigarette shop. He had no family and he lived a simple life as a caretaker of the city’s bird conservatory. He spent his time looking at birds and their absurd little worlds through his binoculars. Those were not just any binoculars but a special edition released by the ‘India Telescope Shop’ in 1947, the year of India’s independence. It was the only thing he inherited from his father and now in his absence, these binoculars guided him in life.
Two days before his grand journey, he lost his most prized possession. He woke up on that dreadful Saturday morning and for the life of him could not find the binoculars anywhere in his home.

For the longest time, he asked every single person and checked every space that his eyes could spot. He could have forgotten to breathe for a minute but not his dearest binoculars. His unsuccessful search devastated and exhausted him.

Instead of sitting in grief, he decided to go in search of the same pair at India Telescope Shop in New Delhi. This was the second train journey of his life. He didn’t want this to become another journey to surrender his father's last remains.
3 days passed and Prem finally returned to Ranchi. He found Aarju playing near the station and finally decided to check with him about the fuss he created last time he saw him.
Aarju was 8 years old and had the creative ability to find old kites on streets and transform them into new kites. As soon as he saw Prem, he ran to him with the biggest smile on his face.
The little boy asked him, ‘Where did you go? Did you find those red goggles of yours?’

Prem’s slouch deepened and today he didn’t even have the heart to correct Aarju. It didn’t matter that they were binoculars (not goggles) because he may never find the same pair again. He found many more advanced versions but not the burgundy red ones with the intricate wood like details.
Aarju felt that asking this question was futile. He told Prem to wait right there as he went to fetch something for him.
When he returned, he had a box with him. Prem thought it was a prank or food and none of those options interested him at the moment.
Aarju pushed him to open it and hesitantly Prem obliged. When Prem opened the box, he was awestruck with tears in his eyes.
He saw the same binoculars’ replica made with thermocol, cardboard, and red familiar pieces with the same intricate wood work. They looked completely alike and not alike at the same time.
There was a note in that box-
Dear Prem,

We found your old binoculars completely shattered near the local dustbin and decided to reinvent them. We tried our best to recreate your binoculars using everything we could find. We miss uncle too and we were just as fans of his binoculars as you were. We are sorry about what happened. I hope you can remember him and see the world from a new perspective through these.
Best,
Aarju and Family <3
These DIY binoculars may not be as functional but when he looked at the world from those glasses, it became rosy.

title: Raja aur uske saathi
paragraphs: There once was a charming prince who loved to sail. Every morning, he would wake up at dawn and, with his army of furry dogs, go to the shore of the island. One by one, all the dogs would hop into the boat, and the prince and his army would be off in search of an adventure.
This was his favourite time of the day because he could be alone at sea and find simplicity in the breeze and the company of his best friends.
Back on the island, his life revolved around ensuring there were enough resources for everyone, protecting his people, and making sure they lived both in peace and with ethics.
This was his time to simply be a person who valued the beauty of the world he protected with everything he had.

Some days, he found fish and shared them with the entire island. Other days, he sat in silence as all his six dogs - Barfi, Badal, Badshah, Babul, Bulbul, and Batik - napped peacefully. He would write poetry alone to soothe the romantic inside him.
But when he was on the water, he allowed himself to feel its movements but never showed too much emotion.
Today was special, though he didn’t know that yet.
Like any other morning, he got onto his boat, and behind him followed his furry army, one after the other, with huge smiles on their faces.

Barfi
Badal
Badshah
Babul
Bulbul
Batik
All on board!

As he began to sail and started humming his favourite ballad, his boat came to a standstill. Out of nowhere, as if someone had played the wrong note, the breeze simply stopped and all the dogs woke up. The boat had decided to hit the brakes, far, far away from the shore.
The morning music stopped, replaced by the collective barking of the six dogs.
‘Badal stop eating Barfi’s tail’
‘Batik don’t scare Bulbul, she is running to the edge of the boat’
‘Bulbul no, not the water’
‘Badshah stop shouting in the air, no one is listening’
He was so confused and, maybe for the first time in a long time, didn’t know what to do as all the dogs started running in panic. He was scared to lose them to the water.
He was a prince, after all, so he decided to take a long breath. He realized it was not as if he were drowning yet…it could have been much worse.
As he stood by the side of the boat, trying his best to find some calm in the chaos, a lovely mermaid started circling around it.

He had only heard in the islanders’ stories that a beautiful mermaid named Aurora lived here. He couldn’t believe his eyes. She was ethereal, with sage green fins and silver streaks running across her body. All the dogs collectively again took a decision to stop barking and look at the magic in front of them.
As she swam, all the small fish of the sea came too. They glided peacefully around her, whistling and jumping as they saw her.

Then, out of nowhere, he saw the fish and the mermaid twirling in a circle while releasing water from their mouths like a fountain. They looked graceful and absurd at the same time. The prince and the dogs forgot all their panic and started laughing at the spectacle in front of them.

Looking at the mermaid and the fish, they too started twirling and dancing with each other. The scene felt straight out of a Disney movie, and for a little while, the prince forgot about the island, his duties, and everything waiting for him back on shore.

When the breeze finally returned and the boat began moving again, he sat quietly with the dogs around him and had the biggest smile on his  face. Nothing about his life had really changed, and tomorrow he would still have the same responsibilities waiting for him, yet he felt lighter.
This morning always stayed with him.It reminded him that even in a life filled with duty, there was still room for something unexpected, silly, that belonged only to him.

title: Sunny ne ab kya kar diya?
paragraphs: This is the story of a rainy day in Boston, a very ordinary occurrence in the city of universities. On a random weekend in late September, the rain gods decided to disrupt everyone’s lives by showering left, right, and center. The weather here also tended to choose the weekend to visit Boston. What a sadist!

There was a girl, Sunny, who had just moved to live a little away from downtown. She loved her new house and always ended up spending an absurd amount of time indoors. She loved the pond, so every other chance she got, she waddled her way to it.

This weekend, as the world prepared to cocoon in their abodes, she decided to stretch her body and touch grass. She didn’t have an umbrella or any understanding of how time passed, or even how to get to a place on time.

Given this, obviously, she decided to book an early afternoon Pilates class 30 minutes away from her home, on a day when the T was shut. And she obviously got late while labouring to make sandwiches from bread, her favourite food, and obviously, in her lateness, she didn’t even get a chance to eat them.
What a menace!
Yes, she is not the most efficient planner or executor, but she has this unique ability to find stories in all her experiences.

In this particular adventure, as the rain gods melodiously sang and her feet failed to catch the bus in time, she found herself immensely discouraged because she not only failed to get one thing right, she also lost money. Her financial loss was an outcome of missing her class, trying to book an Uber and then changing her mind only to pay cancellation fees. Also, these damn late fees!

She contemplated going back home and sulking, a very enticing option given the circumstances. But she was an adventurer, and this ending was unacceptable to her. So, she started by taking a minute to feel all her despair, and then she jumped into action.

She found a way to waive all her late fees and found another class that she could book later on. She found another bus that could take her there, and she found a cafe where she could have a solo date as she waited for her class later on.
The day turned out better than she expected. But in this adventure, and all her other adventures, more than the ending… Sunny valued the presence of her companion - Jamon.

She thought of Jamon in health and in sickness, in moments of missed buses, in the high of winning the Mafia game, and in every moment her heart felt something new or familiar. In all her adventures, she loved ranting about and celebrating the unfolding of events with Jamon. Even when he was not with her in person, he was always a witness and companion to the madness and the mundane.

Jamon and Sunny felt everything deeply and cared a lot about each other. Sunny would create and find chaotic adventures, and Jamon would lose his mind laughing at the absurdities of it all. Jamon was no less of a menace himself, and Sunny loved having a partner in crime.

Together, Jamon and Sunny lived life one story at a time. Seeing this, even the rain gods smiled peacefully, knowing that not everyone hates the rain and that someone knew how to find happiness despite it.

title: Dukchiki from Bodel
paragraphs: Everyday, Avira and Nirvay waited for the late afternoon slump to arrive so all the adults would leave them alone to the adventure of the day. They were 7 and 10 years old respectively and treated each day as an opportunity to do a new insane thing. They grew up hearing stories of far lands, courageous people, and cute animals, so naturally, they believed that anything was possible as long as you could imagine it.

Today, they decided to re-create the kingdom of the most unique leader in history - Dukchiki. She was the only woman to rule over Bodel, wore the most exquisite sarees, was the most skilled fighter ever known, and treated her citizens fairly.

The siblings saw her pictures in their history textbook and decided to set up her kingdom and roleplay those times in their home. They quietly sneaked into their mother’s wardrobe and started rummaging through her exquisite saree collection. They saw cotton, silk, chiffon, and organza sarees, but nothing shouted the kind of royal they had seen in Dukchiki’s photos. As they were about to compromise with a navy blue peacock-print saree, Avira spotted two heavily embroidered dupattas made of Banarasi silk. Before the words could leave her mouth, Nirvay picked up the dupattas and off the two went.

They dressed Avira in a makeshift saree made from the two dupattas and, as a final touch, put her little pink tiara on her head. Then they focused on making the darbaar for the queen, and what better place than their dining room? They wasted no time and used all their strength to move the dining table to the side. Then it was just them, the chairs, and the darbaar of Bodel.

Nirvay was playing a double role - Dukchiki’s bodyguard and also the old man who came to her for help. Our queen went and sat on the chair at the head of the table and commanded the room, ‘Aaj ka sabha shuru kari jayi.’
Nirvay put on a fake mustache and rushed behind the chair to proudly announce, ‘Ji Ranisahiba, har koi ek ek karke raani ke paas ayega aur dur se unko apni takleef batayega.’
Then he removed the mustache and picked up his grandfather’s walking stick to enter through the main entrance.
He took small, gradual steps and hunched his back to get into character as the old, helpless man.
‘Rani, mera naam Gopaldas hai aur mai bahut buddha hai,’ he said, before starting to cough. ‘Meri biwi meri gai lekar bhaag gayi hai. Ab mujhe dudh kaun dega?’
Avira broke character for a second and let a small laugh escape her mouth.
Nirvay looked at her with a big frown and, with that, Dukchiki was back in the room.
‘Don’t worry, Gopaldas, you will get justice in the court of Dukchiki. Aapko pata hai kya ki tumhari biwi kyu bhaag gayi?’
‘Woh kaafi dino se kuch toh bol rahi thi ki the house cow is giving pink milk. I did not question it because mujhe laga woh Rooh Afza de rahi hai.’
‘Hein? Rooh Afza gai se nahi aata hai, Gopaldas! Oh no!!’
‘Achha… par mujhe ab dudh kaun dega?’
‘Tumhari akal aur kaan dono kharab hai, achha hai woh bhaag gayi.’
‘Nahi Rani, mai nahi kho sakta meri gai.’
Raani looked at him with slight annoyance.
So he proceeded to say, ‘Aur apni patni, of course, of course.’
Rani, the little Avira, rolled her eyes and said, ‘Aaj se tum gai ko sambhalna aur uska dudh nikalna seekhoge. Jab tum apni biwi ko dudh dene ke kabil hoge, tumhari biwi ko dhundh denge.’
As the proclamation was made, their parents entered the room and started clapping while desperately trying to control their laughter.
‘Very well said, Ranisa. This sahab will need to learn how to take milk from the cow and serve us,’ said their mom.
Nirvay, fearing that this story might actually come true, threw the walking stick and started running towards his grandparents for the ultimate protection.
All four of them spent their evening running and laughing and filling the ‘darbaar’ with love.
